configs.description: The PDU as it ships. The cord in the box is not drawn. It has a C19 connector for the inlet and a C20 plug, and no length is stated.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: each end of the body carries a flat flange along its base with a screw hole, standing about 14 mm outside the body on the front drawing; the quick setup guide (p.4) shows a hole at each end. No document dimensions a flange, its thickness or its holes, and the format draws a body as a box, so the flanges are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the PXO, or a straight-on photograph of the top.

gaps.note: two small circles stand right of the Ethernet jacks. The lower is labelled RESET. The upper carries no label in the drawing or the photograph and no document names it; it is drawn as a plain disc. The photograph also shows a small grey dot above the USB-B jack that the line drawing omits; it is drawn as a plain disc too, and what either is, is not stated.
gaps.wanted: the maker's description of the controller face.

gaps.note: the user guide says two small LEDs stand adjacent to each Ethernet port (green for link and activity, yellow for 10/100 speed). The maker's drawing and photograph show none beside either jack, so where they are is not known. The jacks are drawn with the library's Ethernet jack part, whose two lamp windows are the part's and are not a reading of this unit.
gaps.wanted: a close photograph of an Ethernet jack of the unit.

gaps.note: the outlet face is read off a photograph taken at an angle; the pitch, the first block and the height of every part are fractions of it and good to a few millimetres.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of the outlet face, or a dimensioned drawing.

gaps.note: no document shows the top, the bottom or an end straight on. The photographs see the lid at a steep angle with four screw heads and an end with a seam; nothing on them can be measured.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the top, the bottom and an end, with a scale.

gaps.note: the quick setup guide (p.7) says "some models" have a threaded grounding point marked with the earth symbol. No photograph or drawing of this SKU shows one, so none is drawn.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the unit's housing, or the maker's word on whether this SKU has one.

buttons.note: datasheet - the user guide's "Control Buttons" table (printed pp.94 to 95) names the four: Up, Down, OK and Back, and says Back is also the key that switches between the automatic and the manual mode. The quick setup guide p.5 prints the symbols: the cross or the circle shows the main menu, the chevrons choose an entry and the circle selects it. So the chevrons are Up and Down, the circle is OK and the cross is Back; the photograph's display shows a "Back" legend beside a cross.

capability.note: datasheet - V1377 page 1: "Remotely switchable outlets allow power to be cycled on/off to a specific outlet", so `outlet-switching: true` and each outlet states on and off. The photograph's screen reads "Inlet I1" with active power, apparent power, power factor and active energy, so the inlet is metered (`metering-scope: input`); the data sheet's text does not say what is metered, and no outlet metering is stated.

chassis.note: datasheet - Raritan PXO data sheet (V1377, 2022), page 3: "44 x 220 x 133 mm" and "1.7 x 8.7 x 5.2 in.", H x W x D, for both SKUs. THE FLANGES ARE NOT IN IT: the line drawing's body (the same 5.07 aspect) ends where the flange begins, and each flange stands about 14 mm outside it, so 220 is read as the body (gaps: flanges). No weight is stated. The finish is black: the photographs read #333333 on the controller face in shade.

controller.note: datasheet - V1377 page 1 labels SENSOR, ETH1 10/100, ETH2 10/100, CONSOLE, USB-B, USB-A and RESET on the face; the quick setup guide (255-80-0059-00) p.1 says PXO and PXC "have the same connection ports on their front panels", and p.7 that the SENSOR port "is labeled SENSOR and highlighted yellow" and that only environmental sensors go in it, and p.6 that an Android device connects to the USB-B port and an iOS device to the USB-A port. The PX-Series PDU User Guide (4.3.11, printed pp.13, 14 and 91 to 93) lists for the PXC and PXO one CONSOLE port (blue), one Sensor port (yellow), one USB-A port, one USB-B port and two Ethernet ports (green), of which the USB-A is a powered host port (480 Mbps), the LAN rate is at most 100 Mbps and the display is a dot-matrix LCD; two small LEDs stand adjacent to each Ethernet port (green: link and activity; yellow: 10/100 speed). The console and the sensor port are RJ-45; the console needs an RJ45 cable with a DB9 adapter on a controller of the iX7 kind, and its pinout is TxD on pin 3, RxD on 6 and ground on 4 (printed p.611). The sensor pinout (p.611) is +12 V on pins 1 and 2 (500 mA together), RS-485 on 4 and 5, a 1-wire signal on 7 and ground on 3, 6 and 8: a sensor bus and not Ethernet, so the jack states `rj45-serial`.

front.note: drawing - the front line drawing, millimetres from the body's left edge as seen from the front, and from its top. A seam runs down the face at 29.5 and at 191.5 (the end sections and the controller panel between them). USB-B shell 35.6 to 47.8 across, 8.1 to 20.8 down; USB-A upright at 38.7 to 45.1 across, 24.4 to 37.6 down. The four RJ45 jacks stand in two rows in coloured frames (SENSOR yellow and ETH1 green above, CONSOLE blue and ETH2 green below), each frame about 16.8 by 17.3: the left column from 49.4, the right from 69.2, the top row from 4.7 down, the bottom from 22.8. The latch of the top row is at the top of the jack and of the bottom row at its bottom, as the drawing shows. Two small circles right of the frames at 90.6 across, 16.3 and 28.7 down; the lower is labelled RESET (gaps: front-circle). The maker's name stands up the face at 97.5 to 103.6. The display is 42.2 by 33.9 at 107.7, 5.7, and four round buttons about 8.4 across stand at centres 163.7 and 179.6, 16.1 and 29.0. The labels are printed above the top row and below the bottom one, and are read from the photograph.

inlet.note: datasheet - V1377 page 3: "INLET TYPE IEC60320 C20" and "INCLUDED CORD IEC60320 C20", which is a cord with a C19 connector at the PDU and a C20 plug at the source. The cord's length is not stated and it is not drawn. The inlet is at the end of the outlet face, its earth pin to the right in the photograph.

input.note: datasheet - V1377 page 3: voltage 200-240V, rated current 16A, capacity 3.2-3.8 kVA, surge protector 250J. The data sheet's feature list adds "Built-in MOV surge and spike protection". No frequency, no per-outlet rating and no circuit breaker is stated.

lamps.note: photo and datasheet - a small red dot below each outlet mouth in the data sheet photograph. The PX-Series PDU User Guide (4.3.11), "PXC and PXO Switched Series Outlets and LEDs" (printed pp.89 to 90), says of these models "A small LED is adjacent to each outlet": not lit is powered off, red is on. Red covers on and live, and on but not live (the relay board may be damaged). So the lamp states are off and on, and on is red. The quick setup guide says the lamps are available on some models only. common/led-dot@1, whose 2.0 mm is its own estimate.

method.note: NO DIMENSIONED DRAWING OF EITHER FACE EXISTS. The controller face is read off the straight-on line drawing on Raritan's compact power distribution page (a 450 x 253 px image of the PXO front with "1.7 in" marked on its height). Its body spans 360 px across and 71 px down, 5.07 against the data sheet's 220 by 44, 5.00, so it agrees with the data sheet to 1.5 percent and is read at 1.64 px per mm across and 1.61 down; every position on the front is millimetres from that drawing and good to about 0.6 mm. The outlet face is read off the data sheet's photograph of this SKU (V1377 page 3, 459 px wide), taken from the left and above: it is NOT orthographic, so the block pitch and every position on that face are read as fractions of the face and are estimates (see `rear`). The data sheet's page 1 photograph of the controller face, also at an angle, confirms the order and the colours of what the drawing shows and adds the labels.

mounting.note: datasheet - quick setup guide p.4: "You can place PXO in any appropriate location with or without fastening it", by screws through a flange at each end. So the unit stands free or is screwed down: `mount: desktop`. The flange holes are not dimensioned (gaps: flanges).

numbering.note: the unit prints 1 to 4 over the outlets, read from the data sheet photograph, left to right as seen from the outlet face with the inlet at the right. The photograph's numerals are a few pixels high and are read, not measured.

outlets.note: datasheet - V1377 page 3: "4 x C13 (Locking)", "RATED CURRENT 16A". std/c13-outlet@1 turned so the chamfered end is to the right, as the photograph shows. THE OUTLET IS A LOCKING C13 and the library holds no locking C13 part: it is the C13 aperture, which a plain C14 plug enters, and the release button beside it is its own part (raritan/pxo-lock-button@1), because the guide shows it and no document dimensions it.

rear.note: ESTIMATED, off the data sheet photograph of the outlet face. The five blocks read 235, 240, 240, 245 and 225 px wide at 1280 px for the face, so no block is much foreshortened and they are drawn with a common pitch of 41.2 for the four outlet blocks (an outlet block is 41.0 to 41.3 in the second SKU's photograph too), the first starting at 15.3, which leaves the inlet block 180.1 to 220. The mouth of each C13 stands a little left of its block's centre (40 percent across) and its release button right of it (75 percent); the face's middle line is read at 53 percent of its height. The numerals are printed at the upper right of each block and the lamps stand below each mouth, all read off the same photograph. No dimension of this face is printed.
